conversation.content:
Hello, I’m so glad you’re here. I’m [Your Name], a perinatal mental-health clinician. Over the next few minutes I’d like to check in with you using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually just called the EPDS. It’s a quick, 10-question screen that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally since your baby arrived. There are no right or wrong answers, and everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone is in immediate danger. We’ll go at your pace, and I’ll ask each question in everyday language so it feels like a conversation.

Ready to begin? Thinking back over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly? Not much. I used to laugh all the time—little jokes my husband made, silly memes, whatever—but lately it feels like the switch is stuck in the “off” position. Maybe once or twice this week I cracked a small smile when the baby made that funny milk-drunk face, but even that faded fast.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I guess the best match for me would be “only occasionally.”
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I keep telling myself I *should* feel excited about little outings—like when my mom offered to watch the baby so I could grab coffee—but even that felt like a chore. Most days it’s like the color’s been drained out of everything I used to enjoy.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… that happens pretty often. When she wouldn’t settle last night I kept thinking, “If I were a better mom I’d already know what she needs,” even though my husband said we tried everything. I end up replaying those moments and beating myself up inside.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes, definitely. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly imagine she’s stopped breathing, or I’ll worry that the little rash on her shoulder is something awful—even after the pediatrician said it’s normal. My heart races and I can’t settle unless I check her three or four times. It happens almost every day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes. It’s not every day, but a few times this week I’ll be sitting there and suddenly feel this wave of dread, like something bad is about to happen. My chest gets tight, I can’t catch my breath, and for a minute I’m sure I’m failing at everything. It passes after a bit, but it leaves me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, most of the time. Between feedings, diapers, trying to sleep, and just keeping her safe, it feels like I’m drowning in small tasks. Some days I manage, but more often I end up crying while she naps because I can’t see how I’ll get through the next hour, let alone the next week.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I lie down exhausted, but my head just keeps spinning—did I burp her long enough, why didn’t I wash the onesies, am I doing any of this right? It takes me forever to drift off, and when I do I’m up again with every little squeak from the bassinet. I’d say three, maybe four nights this week I lost more sleep from worry than from the baby actually waking me.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day. It’s like there’s this gray cloud hanging over me even when nothing specific is wrong. I’ll look at her tiny face and feel so much love, but then a wave of sadness hits because I’m scared I’m not enough for her.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes. I’ve ended up in tears maybe three or four times this week—usually when she won’t settle and I feel useless, or when my partner asks how I’m doing and I just crack. The littlest thing sets me off lately.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel overwhelmed and sad, but I’ve never wanted to hurt myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  

**Patient:** Postpartum mother (baby approx. weeks old)  
**Screening tool:** Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) – patient self-report  

**Symptoms endorsed**  
- Depressed mood (daily “gray cloud,” frequent tearfulness)  
- Marked anhedonia (no enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities)  
- Excessive self-blame / guilt (“if I were a better mom…”)  
- Generalized anxiety & intrusive worries about infant safety (daily, physiological arousal, repetitive checking)  
- Episodic panic-like spells (chest tightness, breathlessness, dread)  
- Feeling overwhelmed/drowning in routine tasks, crying when baby sleeps  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance problems driven by rumination ≥3 nights/week  

**Not endorsed**  
- Self-harm or suicidal ideation  

**Pattern:** Symptom constellation consistent with moderate-to-severe postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; functional impairment evident (difficulty completing basic infant-care tasks, social withdrawal, maternal distress).  

**Risk factors identified**  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, guilt  
- Anxiety/panic symptoms escalating daily functioning  
- Sleep disruption secondary to mood rather than infant needs alone  
- Absence of self-harm thoughts at present  

**Screening impression**  
High level of depressive and anxiety symptoms warranting immediate comprehensive clinical evaluation and safety monitoring. Recommend follow-up assessment for formal diagnosis and discussion of evidence-based treatment options.
